subsection: H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance
text: [Abifadel v. Cigna Ins. Co. (1992) 8 CA4th 145, 160, 9 CR2d 910, 920] • [3:676] Letters by the Federal Home Loan Bank Board to Bank's officers and directors ordering them to comply with various operating restrictions and to perform duties owed to Bank constituted a “claim.” [Mt. Hawley Ins. Co. v. Federal Sav. & Loan Ins. Corp. (CD CA 1987) 695 F.Supp. 469, 479-480 (applying Calif. law)] • [3:677] But letters from a state agency warning that Bank was guilty of specific statutory and regulatory violations and threatening formal regulatory enforcement proceedings and a subsequent cease and desist order did not constitute a “claim” against the directors. [California Union Ins. Co. v. American Diversified Sav. Bank (9th Cir. 1990) 914 F2d 1271, 1276-1277 (applying Calif. law)] • [3:678] Similarly, the mere threat of legal action does not constitute a claim. [Winkler v. National Union Fire Ins.
